title: Highland Sword Dance
summary: In the Highland sword dance two swords lie crossed on the floor and the dancer, in kilt and bonnet, steps in the four spaces between the blades and springs over the cross, keeping time with the pipes without touching the steel. The arms are held high in an arch and the toes are pointed.
howToPlay: Two swords lie crossed on the floor. The four spaces between the blades, and the cross where they meet, are the five places: Back, Left, Right, Front and Cross.
A ring closes on a place when the foot should land there. Tap the place as the ring closes and the dancer steps into it.
Cross is the spring over the blades. Start with the four quarters, then try the quick step.
rules: A tap right on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and taps with no ring open cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through, in groups of four beats.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the dance, not a competition set.
heritageNote: The dance is performed at Highland gatherings and competitions in Scotland and by Scottish communities abroad. It is shown here as dance and skill, never as real fighting.
